how.description: How the person proved who they are: the sign-in connector, or recovery.

class.description: The class of the session the sign-in opens: interactive for a person at a browser, agent for software that keeps its own refresh token and works in the background. Absent on a refusal and on a sign-in to the console.

deadline.description: The latest the session the sign-in opens may live, however often it is refreshed: auth_time plus its class's absolute limit, shortened by its resource's.

reason_code.description: Why a refusal was given, as a code: unknown_audience, not_admitted, subject_token_refused, directory_unavailable and the like. Only on a refusal.

audience.description: The client or audience the caller asked for. Only on a refusal.

missing_requires.description: The groups the audience requires, any of which would have admitted the caller, that the caller does not hold. Only on a refusal.

held_groups.description: The groups the policy evaluation gave the caller. Only on a refusal.

admitted.description: Whether the evaluation admitted the caller to the audience. Only on a refusal.

admitted_by.description: The required groups that admitted the caller, when one did. Only on a refusal.

directory.description: The state of what the groups were read from: live, held (the last answer, while the directory is unreachable), unavailable, or not_applicable. Only on a refusal.
